Is an Energy Truce Viable in the Ukraine War?
news.summary_en: An energy truce in the Ukraine war before winter would serve Kyiv, Moscow, and global markets, yet past pauses have repeatedly broken down. A deal can hold only with a narrow target registry, independent satellite-based verification, and graduated responses to violations.

news.title: The Terrorism Threat to the 2026 Midterm Elections: What the Data Tells Us
news.summary_en: Terrorists have targeted U.S. elections in each of the past several cycles, suggesting that similar violence around the 2026 midterm elections is possible. CSIS experts analyze the data to assess the potential threat.

news.title: EU-China Relations Face an Existential Test, but Escalation Is Not Inevitable
news.summary_en: On July 28, the Chinese Ministry of Commerce published its “Position on the So-called Excess Capacity Issue” to rebut foreign concerns about Chinese overcapacity, signaling a renewal of tensions for upcoming EU-China trade negotiations.

news.title: Wrong Place, Right Line: Interregional Transmission as a Hedge Against Uncertain Large Loads
news.summary_en: Data centers and other large loads are reshaping U.S. electricity demand, but where and when they will materialize remains deeply uncertain. This piece argues interregional transmission offers a resilient hedge against that uncertainty in transmission planning.
